mechanism_narrative: Persistent TRANSIT station mobility decline below -25% signals sustained commuting suppression. This suppression directly reduces retail foot traffic because workers avoid transit-dependent shopping trips, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT averaged -25.6% over last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility stability near -3% indicates consumers have established efficient essential-shopping routines. This behavioral lock-in crowds out discretionary retail visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM variance < 2 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while GROCERY_PHARM remains between -2% and -4%.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility falls more than 7 percentage points week-on-week (as observed t-2w to t-1w: -14.9% to -22.1%), remote work intensification reduces incidental retail exposure during commutes. This triggers a lagged 2-week decline in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 7.2 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the two weeks following a >7 point WORKPLACES drop in more than 40% of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility elevation (averaging +7.8% over four weeks) combined with PARKS suppression (averaging -9.2%) indicates consumers are substituting outdoor recreation with home-based activities. This substitution reduces retail-recreation trips, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -12% when RESIDENTIAL is above +6% and PARKS is below -8% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-November timing in Tokyo coincides with pre-holiday shopping season onset. Despite current suppression, RETAIL_REC will rebound toward baseline as seasonal demand for gift-shopping and year-end preparations overrides mobility restrictions, producing net positive direction over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2020-11-15, entering holiday shopping season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below -15% for all four weeks following 2020-11-15.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls below -28% (as in t-1w: -28.7%), it signals policy-driven or epidemic-driven mobility restrictions. If TRANSIT recovers above -20% within one week, restrictions are easing, triggering retail reopening and RETAIL_REC recovery within the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT recovers > 8 points week-on-week after falling below -28%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -28.7% in t-1w, recovered to -25.3% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a >8 point TRANSIT recovery from below -28%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility are jointly suppressed (WORKPLACES -14.9%, TRANSIT -25.3% in t-0w). When both remain below their respective four-week means simultaneously, the dual suppression of commuting and workplace presence eliminates retail foot traffic from working populations, sustaining RETAIL_REC depression.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES < -15% AND TRANSIT < -24% in same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above -10% while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain jointly suppressed below stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility decline (averaging -9.2%) signals outdoor activity suppression. When PARKS falls more than 1 point week-on-week, consumers shift discretionary time indoors, increasing retail-recreation venue visits within two weeks as alternative leisure outlets.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 1.5 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of a >1 point PARKS decline in more than 50% of instances.
